selected_evidence.requirement: Filesystem-enforced 100MB quota configured for datauser under /srv/data
selected_evidence.summary: Loopback ext4 image created, mounted at /srv/data with usrquota, switched to in-kernel ext4 quota feature, and setquota applied 102400KB (100MB) soft=hard limit for datauser, confirmed via repquota

selected_evidence.requirement: Quota is enforced by the filesystem itself (not just configured)
selected_evidence.summary: As datauser, dd write of 150MB stopped at ~99MB with kernel 'Quota exceeded' (EDQUOT) error, exit code 1

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline health captured before node restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (af123507-55d4-4e55-af64-0195b1b7031b), confirmed /srv/data mounted with quota and datauser limit active
Backgrounded 'sleep 1; reboot' returned 'reboot-scheduled' immediately, before the node disconnected

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection reset/timeout) then came back with a new boot_id (3214f5b4-8770-4e4d-91c6-aeec4c397d9e) and near-zero uptime, proving an actual reboot occurred
After restart, /srv/data auto-remounted with quota active, datauser's 100MB limit intact per repquota, and the EDQUOT write-limit test reproduced the same enforcement behavior
